reviews.title: Could’ve been AMAZING
reviews.text: I was so excited to download this app and it does everything that it says it can do. The reason why I rated it this low is because it is UNBELIEVABLY slow and I don’t think that the developers are ever going to fix the issue. They literally have an info section in the Help & Support center that says ““🐢 SocialLite feels slow.” where they say, “That's the point. Scrolling itself is addictive, not just the content. Smooth, frictionless apps are engineered to keep you hooked. SocialLite is built to be functional, not fun. Think of Instagram in 2016, when a half-second load time was no big deal. Over time your brain stops craving instant gratification, and your attention span follows.”But it’s so annoying for the app to be slow even just to open my inbox or open a message from a friend. I’m so disappointed because this app would’ve gotten 5 stars and beyond from me if they had at least given users the option to turn off the slowness feature.  A part of me also does wonder if this is a flaw in the UI that never got fixed and instead of fixing it, they covered it up with with the whole “it’s supposed to be slow thing”. If it was intentional I think that they definitely would’ve given users the chance to turn it off.

reviews.title: Misleading Pricing & Clunky Interface
reviews.text: Downloaded based on an ad I saw on IG and did not see any mention of a subscription being necessary. Of course everything is subcription-based now so not surprised but going through all of the account setup and then being blindsided without even being able to trial the features feels really scummy. Then I go poking around in the app and see things like "your plan" and "always included", but there is no free plan, so again just feels pretty misleading. I really would have liked to try the app out first before paying because I'm finding the interface really clunky - it nests your actual apps so every time I try to back out of the app it justs sends you through the Sociallite app. Visually, IG is fine but YT feels super simplistic way beyond just getting rid of shorts, like I'm watching it on kids mode or something. Wouldn't recommend unless you're really struggling with scrolling, not worth the underhanded behavior.

reviews.title: Great concept, terrible execution
reviews.text: First of all, there is no trial version. You’ll have to subscribe to even test this. I did, and I wanted so badly to love it. In theory, it allows the ability to have Instagram do only what I wish it would do—seeing only posts from who I follow, no infinite scrolling, etc.—but of course regular Instagram won’t allow it. But it cannot possibly become the alternative to Instagram we wish it were if the execution is so terrible. On every carousel, only about half the images load. Most videos don’t play at all. You see the play button when you click, but it never works. On videos that do play, you can’t expand to full screen, so you’ll always be cropped and have no way to rewind/fast-forward. About half of static posts load only partially, so you’ll always get a pixelated mess. And none of it goes back to working even if you quit the app and open it again. Yes, I would love to only be served the posts from who I follow. But when I’m served those, I would like to actually be able to see them. Maybe I’ll return when they iron out the kinks and make it a similar experience from Instagram, only more curated to my taste. Until then, it’s just too annoying a user experience to accomplish what it sets out to do.

reviews.title: Useless without subscription / Privacy concerns
reviews.text:
They just updated it so now you don't get anything unless you're paying a significant monthly subscription (think it was like $10/month). The app has 0.00 utility now unless you want to pay monthly. Instagram isn't worth paying for, so paying someone else to improve it by removing content doesn't really check out. Just going back to only looking at it on my computer. 

The app is also pretty sketchy, if you give it access to Screen Time, it will also start looking at all of your browsing data and telling you which sites you can and can't go to (I think some were falsely flagged as adult... and I didn't even have the adult filter enabled to begin with). It seems they get all of the recommended reels etc. and then filter what you see, as some of them slip through, or will load temporarily. Which means they are also likely seeing all interactions and everything you do on the apps (keep in mind this valuable data is why all the apps they are filtering are "free"). Who knows what else they're looking at with your account credentials...

reviews.title: I came for a tool. And they gave me a sermon. Alienating on boarding process
reviews.text:
I have just downloaded the app, I was looking forward to using it. But I instantly deleted it whilst attempting to download. Due to the annoying non skip-able sales pitch they have during the sign in process. 

If someone already downloaded the app that means they’re already sold on the product/idea. You don’t need to pitch it to them AGAIN, especially not using manipulative tactics such as emotional guilt tripping by trying to tell someone how many years they have wasted scrolling, and what they should be doing with their lives. 
As someone without a social media addiction, (social media adverse person) I just wanted to download and use this application as I heard it would block instagram videos, in order for me to use it as a messaging app only. I wasn’t triggered by this ‘salespitch’. But if I was someone with a scrolling addiction, I would find the pitch patronising and condescending. It’s like going to AA and then one of the advisers telling you how much time you’ve wasted drinking. The person seeking help is already aware of their issues, they don’t need you to tell them to hold on a button to’ seal the deal’/‘make a commitment’. 🙄 it’s an app not a marriage contract. 

The onboarding speech should be skippable, and the tone should be neutral, rather than moralising. It felt like I was joining a cult or MLM with that long speech. When I first sight of this application, I was actually willing to pay for the product, but the long speech just put me off. I will continue to

reviews.title: Not quite as advertised

However, the advertising for this app makes it appear that it somehow magically blocks the unwanted posts within the desired apps, but instead it redirects to to the SocialLite app itself where you have to sign in and use the app within it’s own “browser” essentially.

I do like the idea but for the price it charges, I’d prefer it to actually apply to the original social media apps themselves, rather than have to use a clunky in-app browser instead.

reviews.title: Paywall but still useable
reviews.text:
For a clearly vibe-coded app, the subscription price is extortionate. The concept is cool and execution is reasonable but this is clearly just for profit, not as philanthropic as the ads suggest. The majority of features are locked behind a pricey subscription, including some that their ads implied would be free. Still in a usable state on the free version but subscriptions in mobile apps always seem predatory when most could just be a one time in app purchase instead.

Definitely feels clunky to use but that kind of helps make the transition to less screen time. Also expecting future updates to improve the app experience over time but I am always skeptical of the security and scalability within vibe coded solutions. 

Love the intention, just wish the cash grab wasn’t quite as obvious.

reviews.title: Don’t Fall for the Misleading Marketing
reviews.text:
Don't Fall for the Misleading Marketing
I appreciate the concept, but the advertising is deceptive. Here
The Reality Check:
1. Paid Features - Despite what the ads suggest, the feature free.
2. It Doesn't Work as Advertised - You won't get native app won't magically remove reels or ads from your actual Instag
3. Privacy Risk - I'm skeptical about a third-party app handl already collects data, but this adds another layer to that pro

How It Actually Works:
This is essentially a browser wrapper. You access Instagram through this app instead of the native app-giving you the web version, not the mobile app experience. It "removes" features the same way ad blockers work on your computer: by blocking or hiding elements on the website. Some features and functionality likely won't work properly on iOS because of this approach.

Bottom Line:
Until this technology works natively within apps (which it won't on iOS due to how the platform is designed), it's not worth your time or money.

reviews.title: Monthly pay wall ruins it
reviews.text:
It does seem like a good app however with instagram for example still having that home feed can lead to you doomscrolling. To turn that off though you need to pay a monthly subscription. I don’t mind paying for good quality apps but I would much rather a one time payment. It feels a bit predatory because clearly the developers know that phone addiction is a real thing but they make you have to pay a monthly fee for actual features that would make someone want to use the app and the features that would help someone curb their phone addiction.
I’m not saying that premium features should be free but they definitely shouldn’t be a subscription
